title: Trading sounds with a caregiver is written as a 6-month skill
summary: By about 6 months, CDC says most children take a turn making sounds after a caregiver's sounds.
body: Language milestones at 6 months include taking turns making sounds with you. The baby vocalizes, then leaves room for the adult, then vocalizes again. That rhythm is social timing, not a word. The page's most means 75 percent or more. Caregiver tips at 2 months already suggest copying the baby's noises; this line is the later checklist item, not those tips. The sheets are not a diagnosis, and another country's chart may use a different month.
